followup: The normalizer extension this verdict preconditioned shipped same-day (commit 7d881194) and was re-probed: see gate-firing-normfix-verdict.json (flags collapsed 12->4 / 5->3, now dominated by genuine unbacked literals; enforce defensible, left as operator decision). The firing rates below are the PRE-extension numbers.
question: How often does the literal-faithfulness gate fire on real extractions at scale, and does the batch-scope default hold up against the stricter source-only scope?
context: The gate shipped default `log` because it never fired on any measured bench arm (evals/results/literal-fidelity-verdict.json): every bench corpus was small and saturated. This run measures firing rates over LongMemEval non-KU haystack sessions in the production note shape, with every claim checked under both corpus scopes. KU haystack sessions are excluded (same guard as distill_datagen) so every KU eval stays clean.
commands: PYTHONPATH=. python evals/gate_firing_probe.py --extractor-url http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 --model teacher --out-tag qwen-27b --limit-sessions 150
server_note: Unjudged probe: fast (TurboQuant) server config acceptable for the 27B teacher arm per evals/qwen_server.ps1 policy; the arm1 arm ran against the deployed sidecar GGUF at :8081. No verdict here depends on bit-reproducibility.

flag_triage.method: All 17 batch-scope flags across both arms inspected by hand against the recorded violation tokens.

hyphenated_unit_vs_bare_digit: 66 (vs '66-acre'; bare digits get no substring match by design)
self_referential_note_index: 12 ('see note 12' cites the claim's own source numbering)

normalization_gaps.note: These are the gate's tokenizer failing to normalize the extractor's legitimate re-formatting ('about two weeks' -> '~2 weeks', '1 to 3' -> '1-3'), not fabricated values.

cases: '10' in a 3-tier taxonomy claim (sharegpt_Qga4bRp_0) — plausibly a derived category count never stated as one number
'11000' in a program-budget claim (sharegpt_rKxzzvF_0) — $11,000 total summed from stated line items; the derived-sum class the design doc predicted

findings: The batch-scope default is empirically vindicated: strict source-only scope would drop 2.4x (arm1) to 1.6x (qwen) MORE claims than batch scope, and the batch flags themselves are ~88% normalization gaps.

Firing rate tracks extractor quality in the expected direction (teacher 2.1% vs distilled sidecar 4.8% of gateable claims), consistent with the gate detecting real re-formatting/derivation pressure rather than uniform noise.
True fabrication rate under batch scope is at most 2/490 gateable claims (~0.4%) across both arms; both suspicious cases are derived aggregates, not invented literals.

decision.enforce: NOT enabled. At current normalization coverage, enforce would drop ~4.8% of the sidecar's gateable claims, of which ~5 in 6 are legitimate. Precondition for reconsidering enforce: extend _norm_literal to handle tilde approximations (~N), plus-suffixes (N+), and hyphenated compounds/ranges (A-B vs 'A to B' / 'N-unit'), then re-run this probe and require the batch firing rate to be dominated by the derived-aggregate class.

caveats: arm1 here is the DEPLOYED sidecar GGUF (per the live compose override), not the 2026-07-06 ladder rung GGUF — firing rates are not attributable to the historical rung.
Sonnet is the primary production extractor; both probed extractors are the local sidecar path. Sonnet firing rates are unmeasured.
Session counts differ per arm (399 vs 147) because the teacher arm is ~3x slower per session; shares-of-gateable are the comparable quantity.
One arm1 and three qwen sessions failed JSON parsing and are excluded from all denominators (recorded in each artifact's `failures`).
